edges.mechanism: Adding high-dose glycine (30-60 g/d) to clozapine gave no benefit; pooled data show worsened positive symptoms (SMD +0.56) and the clozapine-only arm improved more than clozapine+glycine.
edges.evidence: 2 small RCTs plus meta-analysis of 29 trials; low certainty

edges.mechanism: NMDA glycine-site co-agonism; high-dose glycine (0.8 g/kg/d) added to typical antipsychotics, olanzapine or risperidone reduced negative symptoms in small crossover trials; serum antipsychotic levels unchanged (no PK interaction).
edges.evidence: Small RCTs and meta-analyses positive; largest RCT (CONSIST) null; low certainty

edges.mechanism: Glycine-site agonist augmentation is ineffective and may worsen positive symptoms when added to clozapine.
Inherited glycine cleavage defect (GLDC/AMT) with brain glycine accumulation and NMDA overstimulation; treatment aims to lower glycine.
Biallelic GLDC or AMT mutations cause classic nonketotic hyperglycinemia; exogenous glycine adds to the accumulating substrate.
edges.evidence: Genetic series of 578 families; mechanistic inference for supplementation

edges.mechanism: Glycine lowered HbA1c in T2D (5 g/d), GlyNAC lowered insulin resistance 22%, and oral glycine blunted post-glucose glycemia by >50% via a proposed gut-hormone effect; additive glucose lowering possible.
edges.evidence: 1 RCT (n=74), pilot and acute crossover studies; no hypoglycemia reports; low certainty

edges.mechanism: Glycine promotes NREM sleep and lowers core temperature via SCN NMDA receptors; mild sedation in 4.5% of stroke patients on 0.5-2 g/d; additive sedation plausible.
edges.evidence: Animal mechanism plus RCT adverse-event data; no interaction study

edges.mechanism: Both used as sleep aids; glycine does not alter plasma melatonin but has its own sleep-promoting and mild sedative effects, so effects may add.

GlyNAC supplies both glutathione precursors (glycine + cysteine); corrected GSH deficiency and oxidative stress in older adults, uncontrolled T2D and HIV; null primary GSH endpoint in healthy older adults.
edges.evidence: Small RCT (n=24) and open-label pilots from one group; larger RCT (n=114) null; low certainty

edges.mechanism: Betaine is a methyl derivative of glycine metabolized to dimethylglycine and sarcosine and remethylates homocysteine; overlapping one-carbon pathway, combined effects untested.
edges.evidence: Review and RCT metabolomics; no combination trial

edges.mechanism: Collagen is glycine-rich and raises circulating glycine; glycine is a proposed mediator of collagen sleep effects; combined intake adds to total glycine load.
edges.evidence: Scoping review of 22 trials; mediation untested

edges.mechanism: 15 g/d glycine lowered SBP in men with metabolic syndrome; genetically higher glycine associated with lower SBP; additive effect likely small.
edges.evidence: 1 RCT subgroup plus MR; very low certainty

edges.mechanism: Glycine may improve HbA1c and insulin resistance; monitor glucose when combined with glucose-lowering therapy.
edges.evidence: Small RCT and pilot data; low certainty

edges.mechanism: Supplementation raises serum glycine (about 8-fold at high dose) and serine, confounding metabolomic glycine used as a risk biomarker.
Oral glycine raises plasma glucagon and slightly raises insulin acutely.
Glycine 3 g + tryptophan 0.2 g at bedtime lowered serum uric acid (7.1 to 6.7 mg/dL) and triglycerides, possibly via urinary pH.
Absorption of 1.5% glycine irrigant causes TUR syndrome (solute toxicity, dilutional hyponatremia, brain edema); not relevant to oral supplements but same compound.
